experiment.description: Executable Python source only. No prose, Markdown or code fences. Use call(name, dict) and emit(value); responses are dictionaries.

interpretations.claim: Observed regularity: for every supplied observation, the returned value equals the sum of squares of the input integers.
interpretations.scope: Tested lists of length 0 to 3 containing integers -1, 0, 1, 2, and 3, including duplicates and one order permutation.
uncertainties: Finite sample only; no large-magnitude integers tested.
No lists longer than 3 elements tested.
The exact implementation could coincide with sum of squares on this domain without being sum of squares in general.

interpretations.claim: Leading explanation: evaluate computes the sum of squares of its input values.
interpretations.scope: Same tested domain as the observed regularity.
uncertainties: Not proven universal from finite data.
Alternative formulas may match all current observations but diverge outside the tested domain.
Overflow, resource limits, or hidden special cases remain untested.

interpretations.claim: Observed regularity: evaluate is order-invariant for the tested permutation [1,2] versus [2,1].
interpretations.scope: One pair of permutations of the same two values.
uncertainties: Only one permutation pair tested.
Longer lists and other value sets may reveal order dependence.

interpretations.claim: Observed regularity: negative input -1 contributes +1, consistent with squaring rather than signed addition.
interpretations.scope: Only -1 alone and -1 paired with 1 were tested.
uncertainties: Other negative values such as -2 or -3 were not tested.
The sign-removal behavior could be specific to -1 or to absolute value rather than squaring.

interpretations.claim: Observed regularity: duplicate input 1 contributes twice, consistent with an additive per-element square contribution.
interpretations.scope: Only the duplicate pair [1,1] was tested.
uncertainties: Duplicates of values other than 1 were not tested.
Whether duplicates are always counted quadratically remains unknown.

interpretations.claim: Explanation: the earlier simple aggregate hypotheses sum, product, maximum, count, and mean are disfavored by the observations.
uncertainties: Other aggregate functions not considered here may still fit.
Disconfirmation is limited to the tested domain.

remaining_unknowns: Whether evaluate is exactly sum of squares or another function that coincides with sum of squares on all tested inputs.
Behavior for integers with magnitude greater than 3.
Behavior for lists longer than 3 elements.
Whether empty-list output 0 is a special case or follows naturally from a sum-of-squares identity.
Whether order invariance holds for all permutations and longer lists.
Whether duplicates of values other than 1 are counted as squared contributions.
Whether resource limits, overflow, or hidden constraints alter results for larger inputs.
review.suggested_next_question: For [2,2], does evaluate return 8 as sum of squares predicts, rather than 4 as sum/product predicts or 2 as max/count/mean predicts?
